name: Narada Power (Zhejiang Narada Power Source)
headquarters: Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China (US channel: MPI Energy, Grand Prairie, Texas)

ownership.notes: Trades as 'ST Nandu' after an other-risk-warning designation on Apr 30, 2026. No stable controlling shareholder — a Dec 2025 control-transfer attempt collapsed within a week; chairman Zhu Baoyi is the 2nd-largest holder at 6.32% with 90.4% of his shares pledged.

summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Narada is the distressed incumbent of the field — a 30-year telecom/data-center backup-power specialist (#2 globally among Chinese vendors in base-station/DC backup batteries, CNESA 2024) that built a genuinely differentiated grid BESS line (Center L family; GWh-scale semi-solid 314 Ah deployments; an AC/DC-integrated 6.25 MWh 20-ft block; NFPA 855 on a 5 MWh container) and then hit the wall financially: FY2025 net loss RMB 2.64B, a going-concern-qualified audit with an adverse internal-controls opinion, ST designation, 163 frozen bank accounts, and a creditor bankruptcy-reorganization petition filed July 8, 2026. Its US channel (MPI Narada, Dallas — rebranded 'MPI Energy' in May 2026) still sells VRLA and LFP UPS into US data centers, and the company claims top-US-internet end customers. Every commercial read on Narada now starts and ends with counterparty risk.
ecosystemRole: We assess Narada as a cautionary comparable rather than a live US containerized-BESS rival: FEOC status forecloses ITC-linked grid sales from 2026, and the balance sheet forecloses the 10-20-year warranty and O&M promises utility buyers require — but its backup-power heritage matters to the AIDC map. Narada is one of the few vendors with both legs of the AIDC energy stack (inside-the-fence VRLA→lithium UPS→10C AIOn X-Rate→800V HVDC, plus outside-the-fence grid-forming BESS), its MPI Energy channel is a working example of the 'de-branded US beachhead' play, and its distress is actively freeing up backup-power accounts, channel partners, and talent that competitors — including a US-entering Hithium — can pick up.

productsAndServices.name: Center L utility BESS family (Plus / Ultra / Max)
productsAndServices.description: Liquid-cooled LFP and semi-solid containerized BESS. Center L Plus: 20-ft, 5 MWh+ DC block on self-made 314 Ah cells with NFPA 855 certification (announced at SNEC 2025 as among the first 5 MWh 20-ft systems so certified — company-claimed); the workhorse for UK 230 MWh, Greece 130 MWh, Yumen 400 MWh, and Dunhuang 800 MWh. Center L Ultra: 6.25 MWh AC/DC-integrated 20-ft (PCS inside the container), dual-cell 783/587 Ah design, global deliveries from July 2025. Center L Max: 8.338 MWh per 20-ft-class container on 783 Ah 'solid-state' cells, 2000 V architecture — unveiled 2025, no confirmed deliveries as of mid-2026.
productsAndServices.positioning: Second-tier grid integrator by volume with first-tier product claims — the semi-solid GWh-scale deployments and the AC/DC-integrated Ultra are genuine differentiation if delivery performance holds.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct supply and EPC-adjacent contracts; rare in-house 10-year overseas O&M capability (Greece contract) that few Chinese peers offer; also acts as developer on Chinese grid-side stations (Dunhuang).
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Grid-side independent storage (China), utility BESS (UK, Greece, Australia, Europe), 2-8-hour applications.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 2.8 GWh Greater Bay Area semi-solid delivery plan (1.6 GWh due 2026); Center L Max commercialization — both now hostage to the balance sheet.

productsAndServices.name: Data-center / telecom backup power (the heritage business)
productsAndServices.description: HRL/HRXL VRLA series (2V/12V blocks, 15-yr design life) sold in the US for decades through the MPI channel; 512 V high-voltage lithium UPS cabinets (launched 2022; 6C/5C/2C/1C rate models); AIOn Power platform (300-1200 kW per system, 1C-10C discharge); AIOn X-Rate (launched Apr 1, 2026) — 10C ultra-high-rate backup for AI racks on a 55 Ah AIDC-specific hybrid solid-liquid electrolyte cell, >600 kW per cabinet, >1,900 W/kg cell power density, >200,000 pulse cycles @500 ms (all company-claimed); AIOn 800V HVDC and AIOn pod products aligned to NVIDIA-style 800 VDC architecture (CNESA lists Narada among 31 core industry-chain companies for 800 V).
productsAndServices.positioning: #2 globally among Chinese vendors in base-station/DC backup batteries (CNESA 2024 shipments) — this 30-year channel depth, not grid BESS, is Narada's real moat.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to telecom/cloud operators in China (China Tower/Mobile/Telecom, GDS, ByteDance, Alibaba named in company PR); in the US via MPI Energy (Grand Prairie, TX) with US inventory and local engineering.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Telecom, cloud/hyperscale data centers, AIDC racks (10C/BBU-class).
productsAndServices.roadmap: DC lithium capacity 1.5 GWh → 2.5 GWh planned for 2026; company claims 2026 data-center revenue will double (Sept 2025 IR record — pre-dates the April 2026 collapse).

productsAndServices.name: Semi-solid / large-cell ladder
productsAndServices.description: Self-made cell range: 314 Ah LFP; 314 Ah semi-solid (oxide solid-liquid hybrid electrolyte — deployed at GWh scale in the Greater Bay Area projects); 392 Ah (420 Wh/L, 15,000 cycles); 587/588 Ah (430 Wh/L); 783 Ah 'solid-state' (>430 Wh/L, ≥10,000 cycles, IEC 62619:2022 CB certificate); 30 Ah all-solid-state prototype (end-2024). Note: Narada's 'solid-state' large cells are oxide hybrid/semi-solid chemistry in practice — treat the branding cautiously.
productsAndServices.positioning: First GWh-scale commercial semi-solid deployment (claimed world's largest semi-solid BESS award, Aug 2025) — a real technical first among the Batch A field.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Internal consumption for Center L systems; lithium cell capacity ~11 GWh + 6 GWh under construction (company-claimed — treat with caution given capex freeze risk).
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Own systems; company claims 460+ certifications incl. UL9540/UL9540A across the portfolio.

productsAndServices.name: MPI Energy (US channel)
productsAndServices.description: Formerly MPI Narada, the long-standing North American operation (HQ Grand Prairie, TX) — rebranded MPI Energy on May 20, 2026, retaining Narada products while emphasizing 'MPI-designed' systems. Sells HRL/HRXL VRLA and MPLhP/MPLhE LFP UPS series ('UL-certified hyperscale AI data center LFP battery systems'), a 352 kW/5-min cabinet, plus AC/DC-coupled BESS and microgrid offerings.
productsAndServices.positioning: A working example of the de-branded US beachhead: local inventory, local engineering, Chinese cells, and progressively less Chinese branding. No US cell manufacturing.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct and via US distributors (Alpine Power Systems, Solar Electric Supply carry HRL lines — third-party evidence of the installed base).
productsAndServices.roadmap: The rebrand plausibly serves both portfolio diversification and distance from a distressed/Chinese-flagged parent (inference — no source states this explicitly).

recentDevelopments.headline: Dunhuang 200 MW/800 MWh standalone grid-side station completed — Narada as developer + supplier (160× 5 MWh containers, RMB 760M)
recentDevelopments.read: Proof the delivery machine still runs mid-crisis — and a reminder that Chinese grid-side volume is what keeps the storage segment's 27% gross margin alive.

recentDevelopments.headline: Creditor Zhejiang Huazheng Energy Materials petitions Hangzhou Intermediate Court for pre-reorganization + reorganization of Narada; stock jumps 10.6% next day
recentDevelopments.read: The market read reorganization as a path to survival, not a death notice — but court acceptance was unconfirmed in sources, and every long-dated commitment now trades at a distress discount.

recentDevelopments.headline: Progress notice: 163 bank accounts frozen (company + subsidiaries); 66 lawsuits/arbitrations in 12 months >RMB 315M; creditors sought asset freezes of RMB 3.07B (217% of net assets)
recentDevelopments.read: Working-capital paralysis — this is what makes the 2.8 GWh semi-solid delivery schedule and the +1 GWh DC capacity plan doubtful regardless of demand.

recentDevelopments.headline: MPI Narada rebrands to MPI Energy (US) — retaining Narada products while emphasizing MPI-designed systems
recentDevelopments.read: The US channel visibly de-emphasizing the Narada name — consistent with hyperscaler de-risking of Chinese-flagged suppliers and with parent distress.

recentDevelopments.headline: FY2025: net loss RMB 2.642B; qualified opinion with going-concern uncertainty; adverse opinion on internal controls → ST designation; stock falls ~50% over three sessions
recentDevelopments.read: The storage segment itself grew 70.8% at a 27.45% gross margin — the wreckage came from recycling, impairments (RMB 1.46B), and governance. The operating business and the balance sheet are telling different stories.

recentDevelopments.headline: Profit forecast slashed from −RMB 0.89-1.25B to −RMB 2.4-2.8B; Huabo Recycling ceases operations after environmental-permit denial
recentDevelopments.read: The forecast 'face-change' opened investor-litigation exposure; the recycling exit — attempted sale terminated, then forced shutdown — was botched twice.

recentDevelopments.headline: Chairman Zhu Baoyi files to sell up to 1.58% (~RMB 162M) while 90.4% of his stake is pledged; board secretary, one director, and one independent director resign
recentDevelopments.read: Insider selling plus a board exodus in the same month as the loss disclosure — a governance red flag Western procurement teams will weight heavily.

recentDevelopments.headline: AIOn X-Rate launched — 10C AI-rack backup, 55 Ah hybrid-electrolyte cell, >600 kW/cabinet
recentDevelopments.read: Product velocity in the AIDC lane continues through the crisis; the backup business (+7.4% revenue in a collapse year) is the durable core.

recentDevelopments.headline: BNEF Tier 1 energy storage manufacturer, 7th consecutive quarter (Q4 2025)
recentDevelopments.read: Tier-1 listing survived into the crisis — a reminder that BNEF tiering measures bankability of product/track record, not solvency; buyers must underwrite the difference.

recentDevelopments.headline: IR record: ~7.8 GWh undelivered utility backlog (~5 GWh domestic, ~2.3 GWh overseas); DC lithium capacity 1.5→2.5 GWh planned; claims 'top five US data centers' among backup customers; 2026 DC revenue to double
recentDevelopments.read: The pre-collapse plan of record — the AIDC ambition was real and specific, and the US customer claim (unverified third-party) is the single most tantalizing loose end in the file.

recentDevelopments.headline: UK 230 MWh Center L Plus contract + Greece 130 MWh with 10-year in-house O&M announced
recentDevelopments.read: The overseas franchise at its peak — including the O&M wrap few Chinese peers offer. Both now serve as tests of whether a distressed parent can honor long service tails.

recentDevelopments.headline: 2.8 GWh Greater Bay Area semi-solid award (Shenzhen 1.2 GWh; 2× 800 MWh Shanwei) — claimed world's largest semi-solid BESS project
recentDevelopments.read: A genuine technical first at commercial scale; delivery (1.6 GWh due 2026) is the proof point to watch — and the capex is now the constraint.

recentDevelopments.headline: Center L Ultra 6.25 MWh AC/DC-integrated system begins global delivery
recentDevelopments.read: Integrating the PCS into the container leapfrogged most of the 5 MWh field on paper — the differentiation was never the problem; the balance sheet is.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess counterparty risk as the dominant fact about Narada: a creditor reorganization petition, going-concern-qualified audit, adverse internal-controls opinion, ST designation, 163 frozen accounts, and ~80-92% leverage together break the bankability required for 10-20-year warranty and O&M commitments — Western procurement will treat Narada as high supplier-credit risk despite the BNEF Tier 1 listing, and rightly so.

(High confidence) We assess the real moat as the 30-year backup-power franchise, not grid BESS: #2 in CNESA's 2024 base-station/DC backup shipments, a customer list spanning China Tower/Mobile/Telecom, GDS, ByteDance, and Alibaba, and a claimed (unverified) foothold in top US data centers via MPI. The comms/DC segment grew through the collapse — it is the asset a restructuring would preserve or a buyer would want.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the semi-solid GWh-scale deployments and the AC/DC-integrated Center L Ultra as genuine product differentiation — Narada out-innovated its balance sheet. If the 1.6 GWh 2026 semi-solid deliveries land on spec, the technology story survives whatever happens to the corporate entity.

(High confidence) We assess Narada's US position as FEOC-blocked for ITC-linked grid BESS but still shippable for UPS/backup (tariff-burdened): backup batteries inside data centers generally don't claim ITC, so the binding constraints are Section 301 tariffs, DoD-adjacent NDAA restrictions, and voluntary hyperscaler de-risking. The MPI Energy rebrand is the observable adaptation to that last force.

(Moderate confidence) For the Hithium lens: Narada is the cautionary comp — differentiated product, real channel, dead balance sheet — and simultaneously an opportunity map. Its distress puts backup-power accounts, US channel relationships (MPI-style partners), and experienced storage/backup talent in play; a US-entering competitor should track the reorganization outcome for exactly those assets.

relationships.note: AIOn 800V HVDC products aligned to NVIDIA-style architecture; CNESA lists Narada among 31 core 800V industry-chain companies.
relationships.context: Narada's AIOn 800V HVDC and AIOn pod products align to the NVIDIA-style 800 VDC architecture, and CNESA lists it among 31 core industry-chain companies for 800V — ecosystem alignment from the AIDC backup-power side (10C AIOn X-Rate, >600 kW per cabinet), not a named NVIDIA partnership.

relationships.note: The cautionary comp: both legs of the AIDC energy stack, real US channel, dead balance sheet.
relationships.context: Narada is one of the few vendors with both inside-the-fence (VRLA→lithium UPS→10C AIOn X-Rate→800V HVDC) and outside-the-fence (grid-forming BESS) AIDC legs, and its MPI Energy channel is a working 'de-branded US beachhead'. For Hithium it is simultaneously the cautionary comp — differentiated product undone by balance-sheet distress — and an opportunity map: that distress is actively freeing up backup-power accounts, channel partners and talent a US-entering competitor can pick up.

metrics.name: Revenue

metrics.name: Profit
metrics.actual: Net loss RMB 2.642B (loss widened 76.5%); impairments RMB 1.462B (inventory 1.15B); net assets shrank >60% (~RMB 1.4B implied); liabilities ~RMB 14.6B; leverage ~80% (up to 92.1% cited Jul 2026)
metrics.expected: Guidance had been −RMB 0.89-1.25B before the Apr 24 revision to −2.4-2.8B
metrics.result: Catastrophic miss; going-concern qualification, adverse internal-controls opinion, ST label

metrics.name: Trajectory
metrics.actual: FY2024: revenue RMB 7.98B (−45.6%), net loss RMB 1.497B. Q1 2026: revenue RMB 970.6M (−14.8%)
metrics.result: Two consecutive multi-billion-RMB loss years; H1 2026 report not yet located (due ~end-Aug 2026)

financials.commentary: Liquidity per aggregators: near-term obligations ~RMB 6.35B vs cash ~RMB 1.86B; 163 accounts frozen; reorganization petition pending (court acceptance unconfirmed). A March 2026 investor-blog turnaround target (net profit RMB 572-620M, ~RMB 8.9B backlog) pre-dates the April collapse — low confidence. Backlog per Sept 2025 IR record: ~7.8 GWh utility orders. US hyperscaler customer identities remain unverified.
